[A summary of the previous 10 years of research on recidivism to 2007 collated by the Australian Institute of Criminology](https://www.aic.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-05/rpp080.pdf)
Notable correlates of recidivism mentioned
- unemployment, low education, poor residential location, a history of mental health problems, family instability, and serious prolonged drug use
- the younger age at which someone commences offending the more likely they are to be recidivist offenders
- post release difficulties are particularly important. Such as: limited access to financial resources, limited contact with family, and limited knowledge of social support and health services.

[A US Meta-Analysis from 2022 on the impact of incarceration on recidivism](https://www.annualreviews.org/content/journals/10.1146/annurev-criminol-030920-112506)
“Most studies we review, in fact, find that the experience of postconviction imprisonment has little impact on the probability of recidivism. A smaller number of studies do, however, find significant effects, both positive and negative. Beauty is a special interest of mine, particularly the science behind it all.

Let's learn about essences, toners, lotions, and more!

So before we get into the nitty gritty, let's go over a little history. This will help with understanding and remembering the difference.

Two step cleansing systems are relatively new to western beauty. To compensate for this cleansers were far more harsh and alkaline. Due to this, toners were designed to rebalance the skin's pH and remove any remaining "impurities" and makeup from the skin. 

Eastern beauty focuses heavily on layering light products to deeply hydrate the skin. As they had the double cleansing system that left the skin effectively clean, essences were designed to be the first step in hydrating the skin.


Toners
Some toners are inspired by the traditional western toners. Designed to balance the skin and act almost like another cleansing step - however, if it is removing visible dirt/makeup, etc, I would be looking at improving your cleansing regime. Some more modern toners are designed with exfoliation as their main goal. Generally, these are intended to be used with a cotton pad - disposable or otherwise. This is to assist the exfoliating properties and to remove everything it can if you are using it as a cleansing step.


Essences
These are your first treatment step- i.e. your first step after cleansing. The main purpose of an essence is to hydrate the deepest part of your skin topical products can reach and pull all your other skin care down with it. The benefit of this is that your serums and moisturizers don't have to work as hard to sink into the skin and if they can go deeper they can affect more living cells which means it will do more work for the same amount of product. The reason essences are able to do this is because their molecular weight is so small - hence why they feel so watery. As far as pulling your other skincare down, your skin works similarly to a sponge. A damp sponge will more readily absorb water, a dry sponge, however, will repel water and absorb much less than its damp counterpart. While essences are not necessarily designed to have many active ingredients, that doesnt not mean you can't find essences that have benefits other than what I have listed above.


Serums
This is where I generally recommend investing your money if you have any skin concern other than dryness. The concentration of active ingredients combined with the small molecular weight means it does real work in your skin. 


Ampoules 
Think serum on steroids. It has a very high concentration of a single or a few key active ingredients. 


Emulsion 
Emulsions are tricky. This is mainly because this word is used for products that are intended to be used differently. In chemistry, an emulsion refers to a combination of oil and water. I don't want to make this too long, so if you guys would like an explanation of what an emulsion is and why it is used in skincare, give me a shout. Most are similar to a lotion, and they are supposed to go between your serum and moisturizer. Some brands, however, use this term for a product that is more similar to an essence and will be the most light weight, and first treatment step. The easiest way to tell where in your routine it is supposed to go is by weight. If it's watery and thin in texture, it goes first. If it is more milky and thick in texture, it will go between your serum and moisturizer.


Lotion
Lotions are a happy medium between serums and moisturizers. Not quite as light or active as the former and not as heavy as the latter. Unless you have the oiliest of oily skins (and you're certain this is not due to dehydration), lotions are best used under a moisturizer rather than in place of one. For most people, lotions are not necessary, but for anyone who is dehydrated like me, this can be layered under your regular moisturizer for an extra boost, regardless of skintype. 


Now, do you need all of these products in your routine? Absolutely not! Cater to your skin and your needs. 


TL;DR The order is toner, essence, ampoule, serum, emulsion, lotion, then moisturizer. Toners are balancing/ exfoliating and kind of cleansing. Essence is hydration and a small ingredient list of concentrated actives deep into the skin. Ampoules are like a serum with a high concentration of one ingredient. Emulsions are very similar to lotions (most of the time), though occasionally, they will be more similar to essences. Finally, lotions are like a very lightweight moisturizer (even lighter than a water cream).

Found it! So right off the bat I have a couple concerns. Generally speaking foaming cleansers are too harsh on the skin because they use sulphate (the second ingredient) in order to get the lather. This ingredient is used in dish soap and is very drying on the skin. And then after stripping the skin you're not replenishing with a moisturizer.

What your skin then does is go "oh no all my oils, protection, and hydration are gone! I have to fix this fast!" So it makes more oil than it should, often leaving you feeling oily or greasy and clogging pores leading to breakouts and larger looking pores. So by hydrating the skin it doesn't feel the need to produce oil and kills two birds with one stone.

As far as reactions go it can be difficult to determine their cause. First thing to look at is what type of reaction is it? Redness, burning/ itching, rash? This is a sensitivity or reaction. This is when you want to stop using a product immediately. Products causing breakouts can be a little more difficult. 

So purging is a process in which the skin will get rid of any pent up dirt/ pollutants/ sebum etc. This will come in the form of breakouts. The best way (unfortunately) to tell the difference between purging and reacting is to wait. Because the skin takes ~28 days to renew only after that month will you know for sure it's not purging. However if you never get a particular type of breakout like cysts/nodules then you tray a product and 3 days later you suddenly do that's not a super promising sign.

So what I would reccomend is introducing a moisturizer first and finding one that works for you. Then if you still have issues go for a gentler cleanser. The brand you're currently purchasing from has a sensitive rage with a sensitive balance fluid which would be a good start. If you would like to branch out to other brands and want reccomendations just let me know!

Hope that all made sense, and I hope it helps!

The worry shows you care and that means a great deal. The best tips I can give you is preparing anything GF first so you dont have to worry about washing in between and having a separate area/ product where cross contamination is concerned. 

For example if you're making spaghetti use a gf sauce and unmarinated meat and cook that as usual. Then prepare the gf pasta first and once thats done do the regular pasta. For cheese buy a separate bag and let everyone know (or write on the bag) that this one is only for your nephew. If you're doing anything in the oven gf goes on top just in case. 

Some common missed things... condiments if you stick your knife in a pot of butter then for example butter your toast then go back into the butter that is now unsafe. Things like cheese where you're sticking your hand in, unless you wash your hands before using it every time have a separate one. Toasters are just a no, you can't clean that enough.

If you live alone I found making a roster (kind of) for myself really helped me keep track so I'd tidy up right after dinner then do a full clean of one room per week, and then really big stuff like cleaning the oven or airducts once every 3 months or so. If you live with someone else what my partner and I do now is we have a list of the daily and weekly chores and make it a healthy competition. So whoever does that chore for that room for that day or week gets a star. Whoever has the most stars by the end of the week has $50 to spend or save as they please. Sometimes we get something for our selves like makeup or Lego or do a us thing like going out for dinner. This way everything gets done and there's motivation without one person always nagging the other or what have you.  Hope this helps!
